subject: Legend does not appear in PCA plot when using plotTangentSpace function, even when legend=TRUE.

messages.author: c4e264f6ba017714
messages.subject: Legend does not appear in PCA plot when using plotTangentSpace function, even when legend=TRUE.
parts:
Dear all,

I just wanted to check if anybody face this problem: even when legend=TRUE is added, PCA plot using plotTangentSpace does not create a legend. When I try to add a legend separately using legend base function, it does not work on the PCA plot although code works perfectly fine on an empty plot.

Is this a problem with Geomorph package and can it be circumvented for now?

Regards
RD

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Legend does not appear in PCA plot when using plotTangentSpace function, even when legend=TRUE.
parts:
Dear Rochishnu,

There might be something inherent with your data that is causing this issue or an issue with the function that is sprung by your data, as the function produces a legend when I use it.  Your intuition to try to add a legend is a good one, and this is how it works with gm.prcomp, a multi-use PCA function that is now available, which allows plot parameters to be adjusted as the user likes.  In fact, plotTangentSpace will be deprecated with the next geomorph release in lieu of better plotting flexibility with gm.prcomp.

If you check out the examples with gm.prcomp, you might get some inspiration for how to add your own legends or vary plot parameters.

Best,
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Legend does not appear in PCA plot whenusing plotTangentSpace function, even when legend=TRUE.
parts:
I did the same thing and it worked perfectly for me.  However, I subsequently made my plot window much smaller and tried again, and the legend disappeared by virtue of being cut off.  You might consider increasing the size of your plot window and trying again.  If that fails, I would recommend reinstalling geomorph and/or R.

This is a problem with plotTangentSpace and why it is being deprecated.  Optimal plotting in R allows layers to be added to existing plots.  Because plotTangentSpace has multiple plots in one (the deformation grids are plots too), everything has to be created a priori and then cannot be adjusted.  If the plot window is too small, the legend might not work right.  

In addition to gm.prcomp, picknplot.shape allows one to generate deformation grids anywhere in the plot without altering the plot.  Here is the general set up:

PCA <- gm.prcomp(coords, …)
myPlot <- plot(PCA)
picknplot.shape(myPlot) # can make as many deformation grids as desired
legend(…) # add a legend
points(…) # add additional points
text(…) # add text in the plot
title(…) # add a title, if desired
# etc…

None of the above can be done with plotTangentSpace. 

The help page for picknplot.shape has more examples with real data.

Best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Legend does not appear in PCA plot whenusingplotTangentSpace function, even when legend=TRUE.
parts:
Rochishnu,

One of the objects returned by gm.prcomp is a vector of singular values, $d, which is the same as eigenvalues.  In the summary.gm.prcomp, these are provided instead of standard deviations but if standard deviations are preferred, one can get the square-root of these values; i.e., sqrt(data_pca$d).

Cheers!
Mike

From: Mike Collyer
Sent: 04 June 2019 17:10
To: geomorph R package
Subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Legend does not appear in PCA plotwhenusingplotTangentSpace function, even when legend=TRUE.

 

Rochishnu,

 

One of the objects returned by gm.prcomp is a vector of singular values, $d, which is the same as eigenvalues.  In the summary.gm.prcomp, these are provided instead of standard deviations but if standard deviations are preferred, one can get the square-root of these values; i.e., sqrt(data_pca$d).

 

Cheers!

Mike



On Jun 4, 2019, at 7:06 AM, Rochishnu Dutta <rochish...@gmail.com> wrote:

 

Dear Mike,

 

You were correct in pointing out the problem of plotTangentSpace when using a smaller display window that is default in R studio. I could get the legend in a larger output window.

 

Anyways, I have also tried using gm.prcomp as you suggested. It is more flexible and I got the desired result using it. However, in its summary it does not give me the standard deviation in the first row that princomp/prcomp provides. Also, data_pca$sdev, does not automatically give me the standard deviations. Is there a way to get the standard deviation with gm.prcomp?

 

Regards

Rochishnu

From: Mike Collyer
Sent: 03 June 2019 17:10
To: geomorph-...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Legend does not appear in PCA plot whenusingplotTangentSpace function, even when legend=TRUE.

 

I did the same thing and it worked perfectly for me.  However, I subsequently made my plot window much smaller and tried again, and the legend disappeared by virtue of being cut off.  You might consider increasing the size of your plot window and trying again.  If that fails, I would recommend reinstalling geomorph and/or R.

 

This is a problem with plotTangentSpace and why it is being deprecated.  Optimal plotting in R allows layers to be added to existing plots.  Because plotTangentSpace has multiple plots in one (the deformation grids are plots too), everything has to be created a priori and then cannot be adjusted.  If the plot window is too small, the legend might not work right.  

 

In addition to gm.prcomp, picknplot.shape allows one to generate deformation grids anywhere in the plot without altering the plot.  Here is the general set up:

 

PCA <- gm.prcomp(coords, …)

myPlot <- plot(PCA)

picknplot.shape(myPlot) # can make as many deformation grids as desired

legend(…) # add a legend

points(…) # add additional points

text(…) # add text in the plot

title(…) # add a title, if desired

# etc…

 

None of the above can be done with plotTangentSpace. 

 

The help page for picknplot.shape has more examples with real data.

 

Best,

Mike




On Jun 3, 2019, at 7:25 AM, Rochishnu Dutta <rochish...@gmail.com> wrote:

 

Dear Mike,

 

Thank you for the alternate suggestion to use gm.prcomp.

 

Regarding the inherent problem with my data, I have tried replicating plotTangentSpace example with plethodon dataset. In this case too the function did not return  any legend.

 

Regards

Rochishnu

 

From: Mike Collyer
Sent: 03 June 2019 16:43
To: geomorph-...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Legend does not appear in PCA plot whenusing plotTangentSpace function, even when legend=TRUE.

 

Dear Rochishnu,

 

There might be something inherent with your data that is causing this issue or an issue with the function that is sprung by your data, as the function produces a legend when I use it.  Your intuition to try to add a legend is a good one, and this is how it works with gm.prcomp, a multi-use PCA function that is now available, which allows plot parameters to be adjusted as the user likes.  In fact, plotTangentSpace will be deprecated with the next geomorph release in lieu of better plotting flexibility with gm.prcomp.

 

If you check out the examples with gm.prcomp, you might get some inspiration for how to add your own legends or vary plot parameters.

 

Best,

Mike





On Jun 3, 2019, at 3:46 AM, Rochishnu Dutta <rochish...@gmail.com> wrote:

 

Dear all,

 

I just wanted to check if anybody face this problem: even when legend=TRUE is added, PCA plot using plotTangentSpace does not create a legend. When I try to add a legend separately using legend base function, it does not work on the PCA plot although code works perfectly fine on an empty plot.

 

Is this a problem with Geomorph package and can it be circumvented for now?

 

Regards

RD
